q-72052.name: Question 1
q-72052.problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.9$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ | $0.9$ |

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a backward difference approximation.
q-72052.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the point $x=-1.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{f(-1)-f(-1-1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{f(-1)-f(-2)}{1} \\  & =\frac{0.1-0.4}{1} \\  & =-0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-343846.problem:
The concentration of a medication in a patient's bloodstream, measured in milligrams per liter, is given by the function $C(t)$, where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the medication was taken. The values of $C(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $1$ | $5$ | $9$ | $14$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $C(t)$ | $18$ | $11$ | $7$ | $2$ |

Approximate the rate of change of the concentration when $t=9$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

The estimated rate of change when $t=9$ is
{{field-1}} milligrams per liter per hour.
q-343846.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{C}^{′}(t)≈\frac{C(t)-C(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=9.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{′}(9) & ≈\frac{C(9)-C(9-4)}{4} \\  & =\frac{C(9)-C(5)}{4} \\  & =\frac{7-11}{4} \\  & =\frac{-4}{4} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $t=9$ is $-1$ milligrams per liter per hour.

Question 19
?

The share price, in dollars, of a rapidly growing company after t years is given by the function R(t), whose graph is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the share price is increasing when t=2 using a backward difference approximation with step size h=1.

a
$6500/year
b
$7000/year
c
$5500/year
d
$6000/year
e
$7500/year
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We use the backward difference approximation formula R′(t)≈R(t)−R(t−h)h, at the time t=2. Applying the above formula with t=2 and h=1 gives

R′(2)≈R(2)−R(2−1)1=R(2)−R(1)1=7000−1000=6000.

So the rate of increase is $6000/year.

A cup of coffee cools over time. The temperature after $x$ minutes, in degrees Fahrenheit, is given by the function $T(x).$ The graph of $T(x)$ is shown above.  

Approximate the rate of change when $x=36$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=11.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=25$ and $x=36.$*

The estimated rate of change when $x=36$ is
{{field-1}} degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
q-343867.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{T}^{′}(x)≈\frac{T(x)-T(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=36.$  Applying the above formula with $x=36$ and $h=11$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(36) & ≈\frac{T(36)-T(36-11)}{11} \\  & =\frac{T(36)-T(25)}{11} \\  & =\frac{44-45}{11} \\  & =-\frac{1}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $x=36$ is $-\frac{1}{11}$ degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
